profile_text.body:
Arm is a for-profit public company founded in 1990 and headquartered in Cambridge, United Kingdom. On its own site it describes itself as providing the compute platforms behind advanced AI, connecting cloud, edge, and physical AI with consistent software, flexible compute, and an ecosystem it says is built to scale intelligence everywhere. The company says its technology delivers performance, efficiency, and flexibility across cloud infrastructure, personal devices, AI-defined vehicles, and robotics, and that it enables scalable orchestration across cloud and edge environments as AI and compute converge.

Among the things Arm highlights are the Arm AI Portal, which it describes as one place for developers and agents to discover optimized models, evaluate performance, access deployment workflows, or optimize their own models for Arm, and the Arm AGI CPU, which Arm's Eddie Ramirez explains the company launched. Arm also points to NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform as an example of how Arm powers agentic AI, and notes that NVIDIA DGX Spark is built on Arm-based NVIDIA Grace Blackwell technology. It cites Arm Create Shanghai and Shenzhen as events where the ecosystem showed work on intelligent applications, and describes real-time, power-efficient edge AI for consumer and embedded devices as well as compute for autonomous machines.
